leading_candidate.name: dovetail
leading_candidate.status: LEADING CANDIDATE, NOT SELECTED — must survive a cold re-read next run before any implementation
leading_candidate.proposed_hook_sentence: Two artists edited the same 3D file at the same time — this merges both of their changes into one file that opens in Blender.
leading_candidate.proposed_demo: three renders side by side: A's change, B's change, and the merged file rendered by Blender itself
leading_candidate.closest_prior_art: Blender PR #151266 blend_diff (diff only; upstream states merging is 'a significantly more complex problem'), blendiff on PyPI (diff only), ifcmerge (three-way merge, IFC not .blend), UnityYAMLMerge (three-way merge, YAML with stable IDs)
leading_candidate.feasibility_verified: bpy 5.0.1 installs and imports here; a script authored, saved, re-opened and CPU-rendered a .blend. Cycles-CPU only (no libEGL.so.1 for BLENDER_WORKBENCH). Saved .blend begins 28 b5 2f fd (Zstandard), so a parser must decompress before reaching SDNA.
leading_candidate.open_question_blocking_selection: the model-driven engineering literature on three-way merging of graph-structured models (EMF Compare, EMF Diff/Merge, academic model merging) has not been searched, and is the only remaining source that could materially overlap the algorithm
leading_candidate.design_question_to_settle_before_milesto: merge on the file structure directly (primitive; bpy used only as an independent oracle) versus merging by appending through bpy (a script, not a primitive)
leading_candidate.prior_art_search_scope: web search (multiple query formulations), GitHub, PyPI, and search-result summaries of the Blender developer tracker and Blender Artists forums. A direct fetch of projects.blender.org returned HTTP 403 in this environment, so the PR #151266 quote is second-hand and unverified.
